uncited: **Volume Data:** Stored in memory according to object coordinates $(u, v, w)$.
**Partition Map:** Defines axis-aligned sets of voxels.
**Intermediate Baseplane:** A 2D buffer corresponding to a specific voxel set.
Its size is determined by the viewing direction and set dimensions.
**Compositing Tree:** A binary tree structure used to combine baseplanes.
**Permuted Coordinates $(x, y, z)$:** The origin is repositioned to the vertex nearest the image plane.
**Baseplane Coordinates $(x_b, y_b, z_b)$:** $z_b=0$ is co-planar with the $xy$-face in permuted coordinates.
**Partitioning:** Divide the volume data set, stored in object coordinates, into a plurality of axis-aligned sets of voxels.
**View Selection:** Select an arbitrary viewing direction.
*   Iterate through voxels $(i, j, k)$ in the sub-volume.
*   Calculate the sheared position $(p, q, k)$ in the baseplane coordinate system.
*   **Overlap Handling:** At the edges of volume partitions, rendering samples might be duplicated if overlapping sets of voxels are not handled correctly.
*   **Baseplane Size:** The size of the baseplane depends on the viewing direction.
The maximum size occurs when the viewing direction is 45° to all faces.
*   **Cursor Handling:** If a 3D cursor is used, its center $c_g(x,y,z)$ is specified in object coordinates.
*   **Time Complexity:** The rendering complexity is $O(V^3)$ where $V$ is the side length of the volume.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Requires memory for the volume data and intermediate baseplanes.
